spans.s: napta = Skt. naptṛ (〔§ 13.4〕), (nearer) descendant: napta-pranapti-kāye (mss.) Mv 〔i.348.9〕, in the crowd of his near and remoter descendants; cf. pranapti.

nāpinī, woman of the barber caste: Divy 〔370.1, 3〕. [] One might be tempted to assume a misreading for Skt. nāpitī. But note Pali nahāminī, Pv 〔iii.1.13〕, repeated in comm. 〔176.1〕 with gloss kappaka-jātikā. Our word looks like confirmation of Kernʼs conjecture, cited PTSD s.v. nahāmin, that the Pali form stands for ˚pin(ī).
